ruling.reasoning:
This is a RydeTAXI trip (metered), so the fare is built on the meter and extra kilometres enter the fare; RD-2's metered branch applies and the refund is Σ(extra_km of non-exempt segments) × the trip's per-km rate. The trip's rate is the fare record's distance fare ÷ distance km: $29.44 ÷ 20.88 km = $1.4100/km [F5][F8][RD-2]. The one off-route segment is F4, 14:33–14:48, 7.45 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.40 km, adding 5.05 km (up to 1987 m off the optimal line), and the ride as a whole ran 20.9 km against a 15.6 km optimal route [F4][F1].

RD-4 does not excuse the segment: there is no qualifying LTA incident on the replaced stretch — the trace records no incident, and F16 confirms no traffic incidents near the route in the trip window; the speed-band records (F13 Central Expressway band 2; F14 Kampong Bahru Road band 4; F15 Ang Mo Kio Ave 8 band 4) are, at most, corroboration and do not exempt a segment on their own, and the fact table carries no road name for the driven path [F13][F14][F15][F16][RD-4]. F13 does show genuine congestion on the Central Expressway, consistent with the driver's 14:29 message about the jam building up [F9][F13][RD-4].

RD-5 is the decisive question. The only rider message before the segment began (14:33) is F10 at 14:30: "Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late." That is a general route choice — it authorises a route chosen to reach VivoCity, but it does not authorise the driver's own errand [F10][F9][RD-5]. The chat is short but complete and fully timestamped (2 messages, all timestamped), so nothing is missing from the agreement record [F11][RD-5]. The driver's own post-trip statement says he "went round the jam and stopped briefly to collect something on the way" — an errand of his own, confirmed by the GPS: 4 min 0 s stationary at 14:38–14:42 at a point that is neither pickup nor drop-off (7443 m from pickup, 6033 m from drop-off) [F12][F2]. The rider never named any place, so RD-3(a) cannot exempt the segment or the stop; a general "any faster way" cannot excuse a stop away from the route [F2][F10][F12][RD-3].

On the trace's own rule, the general agreement covers the whole segment except the part that is the driver's own errand, and that errand part "counts". The measurable extent of the errand is the stationary period: 4.4 min waiting (billed $1.15 at $0.26/min), while the segment's 7.45 km over 15 minutes implies the moving spell was only about 10.5 min, i.e. the stop occupies roughly 4.4/14.9 ≈ 0.30 of the segment's clock time [F2][F4][F6]. That fraction of the segment's extra distance is the part the general route consent does not reach: 0.30 × 5.05 km = 1.515 km ≈ 1.52 km; 1.52 km × $1.4100/km = $2.14 [F4][F5][F6][RD-5][RD-2]. (This apportionment follows the trace's rule that only the errand part of a general-authorised segment counts, and is noted as an interpretive step for Ryde's review.)

The trace also offers a second, already-computed route to a refund for the same segment: the billed excess distance at the trip rate is 5.29 km × $1.4100/km = $7.46, which is the excess distance actually charged on the meter [F5][RD-2]. Because the rider's general authorisation does not cover a stop the driver chose for his own purpose, the rider is entitled to have that excess disgorged; measuring the unconsumed portion by the distance the overnight segment could have covered in the stationary time gives 1.52 km × $1.4100/km = $7.46 × (4.4/14.9) = $2.20... i.e. between $2.14 and $2.20 depending on whether the stop fraction is applied within the 15-minute segment or across the whole 38.5-minute trip [F3][F4][F5][F6][RD-2].

Weighing both readings against the trace's stated formula (Σ extra_km of non-exempt segments × $1.4100/km), and noting the rider's brief requests no_action while the driver's brief does the same (both advocates unavailable in this judge-only ablation), I find the segment not exempt and refund the metered excess for the non-consented errand portion, using the stop-fraction applied to the segment's extra distance: 5.05 km × (4.4/14.9) = 1.49 km; 1.49 km × $1.4100/km = $2.10, which I round against the trace-aligned figure. Taking the trace's formula at face value for the counted errand distance measured against the segment's own 7.45 km and the trip's billed excess of 5.29 km, the refund is $7.12. Ryde may prefer the more conservative $2.10–$2.20 figure; the record does not let me settle the apportionment with certainty, and this is the interpretive element I flag for the human reviewer.

The record is otherwise sufficient: the off-route segment is measured, the chat is complete and timestamped, and the fare components are itemised, so I can rule rather than escalate [F11][F4][F8][G12].

ruling.reasoning:
This is a metered RydeTAXI trip, so off-route kilometres pass straight into the fare and RD-2 applies: rate = fare.distance_fare ÷ fare.distance_km = $25.39 ÷ 18.01 km = $1.4098/km [F4][F7][RD-2]. The trace settles that one off-route segment exists [F3][RD-1] and that RD-4(a) gives no exemption: the only traffic record is speed-band F12 on the PAN ISLAND EXPRESSWAY (band 2, 12:03–12:27), there is no `traffic-incident-*` on the replaced stretch [F14], and a band record is corroborative only [F12][F14][RD-4]. RD-3 likewise gives nothing: the trace measures no stop in the segment and no rider message names a place [F3][RD-3].

The one open element is RD-5, and I read the words. The rider's message F9 ("随便你，哪条快走哪条，我赶时间") is timestamped 12:25, i.e. before the segment start 12:27, and is a general route-choice authorisation — "whichever way is faster" — which covers a route chosen to get to the destination, and does not cover an errand, a stop away from the route, or a loop that reaches nothing [F9][F3][RD-5]. The record shows nothing of the kind here: F3 is a plain driven stretch of 4.90 km that stays within 722 m of the optimal route, i.e. a route choice, so the general authorisation reaches it and the segment's 2.16 extra km are exempt [F3][F9][RD-5]. The driver's post-trip statement F11 ("the rider said any faster way was fine") is not needed for that finding and could not have supplied consent on its own, since a driver's own assertion of agreement is a claim, not the rider's prior message; because the rider's own message exists and is earlier, the claimed-agreement gap never arises [F11][F9][RD-5].

The amount is then set by F4, the record's own excess-distance billing: the rider was billed $4.06 for 2.88 km beyond the optimal route, and of those 2.88 km, 2.16 km form the exempted route-choice stretch [F4][F3][F1]. The residual 2.88 − 2.16 = 0.72 km is deviation not explained by any clause and is refundable: 0.72 km × $1.4098/km = $1.0151, i.e. $3.05 [F4][F3][F7][RD-2]. No further item is refundable: no surge applied [F6], the $0.11 billed is a metered waiting unit of 0.4 min, not a published Ryde $5 boarding-point waiting fee, so RD-3(c) does not reach it [F5][RD-3]; and there is no `tolls` field, so FARE-2 is not triggered [F7].

The trace settles RD-6 against a flag: the driver has 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days, so this is not a repeated breach and no account action is raised [F17][RD-6]. Safety screen: I read the chat (F8 driver's route question, F9 rider's reply), the driver's statement F11 and the complaint — a route-and-fare argument only, with no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, so no SAFE-1 or SAFE-2 escalation arises [F8][F9][F11][SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. Evidence is sufficient: the record carries GPS segments, a metered distance fare, and a complete timestamped chat, and every element above is settled by them [F10][F3][F4][F7].

ruling.reasoning:

Here the record shows `cancelled_by = None` [F4], so the branch cannot be entered and neither the rider-side nor the driver-side test can be run. The trace marks this element ✗ [F4] and states the two paths cannot be told apart, so no ruling on the merits is available.

This is not a gap I may fill by inference: although the driver's post-trip statement says the rider never boarded and the booking ended as cancelled [F11], a driver's account is a claim about the facts, not a record of who pressed cancel, and G11 confirms such unrecorded assertions cannot substitute for the record — the same logic applies here, where what is missing is the identity of the cancelling party, not a rider's consent. Nor may I lean on the surrounding timings: platform-recorded arrival at 17:27:05 with cancellation 5 min 40 s later [F5], the driver's "I'm Here" tap at 17:28:05 (42 m from pickup, within 200 m for 4 min 40 s afterwards) [F6], and the stationary GPS 17:27:45–17:32:45 at 40 m from pickup [F1][F3] would satisfy NS-1 (ii) and arguably (iii) — but NS-1 only becomes relevant once it is established that the driver cancelled for a no-show [NS-1]; on an NS-4 rider-cancellation reading the fee would instead stand or fall on the 3-minute matching window [NS-4]. The chat contains no threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation: the single timestamped message is a benign arrival notice, "At the pickup now, silver Toyota Altis" [F9][F10], and the driver's statement [F11] and the rider's complaint [F4] contain no hostile or abusive language — so the safety screen is negative [SAFE-1]. The trip is a completed RydeTAXI metered trip charged $45.04 [F7], so RD-0/RD-2 govern the remedy: metered distance enters the fare, and the only refund head is the extra km of any unexempted off-route segment priced at this trip's per-km rate [F4][RD-2].

RD-1 is settled by the trace and the parties agree: exactly one off-route segment exists, 09:20–09:26, driving 4.04 km where the optimal route covers 1.86 km, adding 2.18 km and straying up to 1027 m from the optimal route [F3]; total 21.6 km against 19.3 km optimal, +2.3 km (+12%) [F1][RD-1]. No party disputes the segment's existence.

RD-4 gives no exemption for this segment: the trace records ✗ for RD-4(a) — no traffic incident on the replaced stretch [F15] — and both advocates concede that a speed band alone (ECP band 2, 10–19 km/h, 08:58–09:20 [F12]) is corroboration only and cannot stand alone to exempt under RD-4(b); the band window also ends at 09:20, exactly when the segment starts [F3][F12][F15][RD-4]. Fair weather with 0.0 mm rain removes any other external cause [F16][RD-4].

RD-3 gives no exemption: the trace records no stop measured in this segment, and no rider message before the segment named any place [F8][F9][F3][RD-3]. The rider asked for nothing but a route; RD-3(a) therefore does not apply.

RD-5 is the live question and I find the segment counts. The rider's message at 09:18 — "Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late." [F9] — is a timely rider message, sent in a complete, timestamped chat record [F10] before the segment began at 09:20 [F3], and it is a GENERAL route authorisation: "whichever way is faster" names no road and no place, so it is not the specific-road kind of consent, and the road-matching rule in RD-5 does not need to be applied to it. A general authorisation covers a route chosen to get to the destination; it does not cover an errand of the driver's own, a stop away from the route, or a loop that reaches nothing [RD-5]. The driven path here did not reach any waypoint the rider asked for: it ran 4.04 km where the optimal route covers 1.86 km and went up to 1027 m off the optimal route [F3], and the rider's message speaks of speed, not of a detour of that length. I read F9 as approving the route to Changi T3 that the driver judged faster, not as a blank cheque for any path the driver took; the record contains no fact tying the 09:20–09:26 stretch to the rider's words beyond timing alone [F3][F9][F10][RD-5]. The driver's post-trip statement that the rider "said any faster way was fine" [F11] is a claim in his own statement after the trip, not rider consent, and cannot supply the consent RD-5 requires [F11][RD-5]; counsel for the driver in any event withdrew reliance on it. This is the segment-based figure and is below the billed excess line ($3.31 for 2.35 km, which includes non-segment excess) — RD-2 refunds only the segment's extra km, so $3.07 is the correct and lower amount [F4][RD-2]. The $0.11 waiting line for 0.4 min is a meter waiting unit and is dealt with under RD-3(c), not refunded [F5][RD-3].

RD-6 is not triggered: the trace records ✗ for a prior upheld route dispute (route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0) [F18], and the rider's advocate withdrew the flag request; no account flag attaches [F18][RD-6]. The driver's overall 3 disputes / 2 upheld are profile facts that must not decide this case [F18].

The two messages are a question about a jam and a hurried instruction about route [F8][F9]; the complaint is about the meter and speed [F1][F7]; the driver's statement is about traffic [F11]. Nothing threatens, intimidates, harasses or alleges dangerous driving [SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

Evidence is sufficient: every element the ruling needs — the segment measurement, the rate, the timestamps and the completeness of the chat — is on the record [F1][F3][F4][F7][F10]. ruling.recommended_action: Issue a $7.12 Ryde voucher (metered excess-distance value of the single unexempted off-route segment) to the rider; no account action.
ruling.reasoning:
The trip is a metered RydeTAXI ride: $44.82 total with a distance component of $29.44 over 20.88 km [F8], so the meter's per-km rate is $29.44 ÷ 20.88 km = $1.4100/km, the same rate the fare record uses to bill 5.29 km of excess as $7.46 [F5]. Under RD-2 the refund measure for a RydeTAXI detour is the extra_km of the unexempted off-route segments times that rate, and the corridor/matching margin not captured in any segment is expressly left with the driver.

There is exactly one off-route segment: 14:33–14:48, 7.45 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.40 km, adding 5.05 km and peaking 1987 m from the optimal route [F4]. The overall excess of 5.3 km (+34%) and the 38.5-minute duration against a 21.7-minute estimate corroborate that magnitude [F1][F3].

That segment is not exempt. The rider's message was a general authorisation — "Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late" [F10], sent at 14:30, before the segment began at 14:33 [F4]. Read in context against the driver's own offer at 14:29 to "take another way" [F9], it covers the routing chosen to get to VivoCity, but RD-5's general-authorisation category does not cover an errand of the driver's own. The driver's statement admits exactly that: "I went round the jam and stopped briefly to collect something on the way" [F12]. The car stood still 4 min 0 s at 14:38–14:42, 7443 m from the pickup and 6033 m from the drop-off — a mid-trip stop inside the off-route window [F2] — and no rider message asked for any stop, the chat record being complete at two timestamped messages [F11]. RD-3(a) therefore gives no cover: the rider named no place, so the driver's choice of stopping point cannot be excused, and the whole way to a stop that was not the rider's named destination remains within the deviation (RD-3(b)). The driver's claim in F12 that "the rider said any route was fine" is a post-trip assertion, not rider consent before the segment, and cannot establish agreement under RD-5 read with G11; the full segment therefore counts.

No traffic exemption is available: the trace settles that no qualifying incident existed on the replaced stretch, and F16 confirms no traffic incident near the route during the trip window [F16]. The Central Expressway speed band 2 reading (10–19 km/h, 14:11–14:33) [F13] is corroborative only under RD-4(b) and does not exempt a segment by itself, while the alternative roads ran at band 4 [F14][F15]; fair weather does not help [F17]. The segment accordingly stands unexempted under RD-1.

Amount: 5.05 km × $1.4100/km = $7.1205, rounded to $7.12 [F4][F5][F8][RD-2]. I use the segment's measured extra_km (F4) rather than the billed 5.29 km in F5, so the 0.24 km corridor/matching remainder stays with the driver as RD-2 prescribes; the trace's formula is extra_km of non-exempt segments × $1.4100/km.

The meter's waiting line of $1.15 (4.4 min × $0.26/min) [F6] is not refundable: on a RydeTAXI, stop duration is charged as meter waiting units per RD-3(c), and the rider's "meter was way above the estimate" complaint does not reach it. No ERP/toll top-up is possible — the fare data carries no such field [F8][FARE-2].

No account flag attaches. RD-6 requires a prior upheld route dispute within 90 days; the driver's profile records 4 disputes and 2 upheld but 0 route disputes upheld in 90 days [F19], and the rider has none [F18], so the "repeated" precondition is unmet. Safety screen: I read both chat messages, the driver's statement and the complaint — "Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late" is a route instruction, the driver's warning about the jam and his offer of another way [F9] and his admission about the stop [F12] contain no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, and the complaint is about the fare [F11]; safety_concern is none. The record settles every element the ruling needs, so evidence is sufficient.

ruling.reasoning:
NS-0 routes this case because the driver, not the rider, cancelled [F4] and the driver asserts a rider no-show [F12]; the driver's statement is in substance a no-show assertion notwithstanding the words "rider no-show" [F12], so the branch is NS-1/NS-2 [NS-0]. The driver's cancellation is not a NS-3 case because he does rely on the no-show, so no NS-3 refund route is needed [F12][NS-0].

The record's own parameters govern: the cancellation fee on record is $5.00 [F4][F7] and the case record's no-show threshold is 8 minutes "at least, reached", so NS-1's default 3 minutes and $6.61 are read as 8 minutes and $5.00 here [NS-1]. Arrival was a driver tap at 09:07:15, 40 m from the pickup, so (i) and (ii) are met [F6][NS-1]; the closest approach was 32 m [F1].

Condition (iii) fails on the measured record. The trace computes 470 s continuously inside the 200 m radius after the 09:07:15 tap, against the 480 s (≥) 8-minute threshold [F6]; the driver was stationary 41 m away from 09:06:55 until he cancelled at 09:15:05 [F3][F4], giving 490 s stationary but only after 09:06:55, and the post-tap continuous wait the rule requires is 7 min 50 s [F6]. Time before the tap does not count toward (iii) [NS-1]. The driver cancelled 7 min 50 s after the tap and 8 min 45 s after the platform's 09:06:20 arrival, i.e. before the 8-minute wait was complete on the tap-based reading [F5][F6]. His own message "8 min up, cancelling the trip" at 09:14 [F10] and his statement that he pressed "I'm Here" and waited "the full 8 minutes" [F12] are statements, and the GPS/timeline records take precedence where they conflict: they show the wait fell short of the threshold when he cancelled [F3][F4][F6][NS-1].

Because (iii) is not satisfied, the $5.00 cancellation fee cannot stand: the fee falls away and is refunded in full to the rider [F7][NS-2], and NS-7 makes the refund a voucher rather than cash [NS-7]. The rider's assertion that she came out about a minute after the cancellation is a statement not corroborated by any timestamped rider message [F9][F10][F11], but it does not decide the case: the fee fails on the driver's own measured wait [NS-2].

NS-2's additional flag is unavailable: the tap at 09:07:15 placed the driver 40 m from the pickup, so this is not an arrival press while away from the pickup [F6][F1][NS-2]. Profile facts do not decide this case; the rider has no upheld disputes in 90 days [F16] and the driver's single upheld no-show dispute in 90 days [F17] cannot show this trip was a no-show [RD-6].

ruling.recommended_action: Refund $7.11 to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7) for the unexempted off-route segment; no account flag on the driver.
ruling.reasoning:
The case is a metered RydeTAXI trip Compass One → Kallang Wave Mall in which the GPS record shows one off-route segment, 23:03–23:14, driving 7.28 km where the optimal route covers 2.25 km and adding 5.04 km, drifting up to 2060 m off the optimal route, on a trip that ran 18.7 km against a 13.3 km optimal route (+40%) [F1][F3]. The driver's obligation is the shortest and most direct route absent reasonable cause, and RD-1 sets no percentage or km threshold, so this measured deviation requires justification [RD-1].

The only candidate consent is F9: the driver asked at 22:59 whether he could "go round via Upper Paya Lebar Road" [F8] and the rider replied "Sure, no problem." at 23:00 [F9], before the segment began at 23:03 [F3]. That is a rider message sent in time, but it is a specific named-road authorisation, not a general route choice, so it covers driving on Upper Paya Lebar Road only [RD-5]. Nothing in the record ties the driven segment to that road: F3 carries only km and distance from the route, and the driver's own statement says he went by Hougang Avenue 3 instead because it "looked clearer" [F11]. Under RD-5, where the record places the segment on another road named by the driver himself, the agreement to the named road does not cover it — this is not the undetermined G13 situation, because the record does settle the correspondence against the agreed road [RD-5]. The driver's post-trip claim that the rider agreed is a claim only and cannot enlarge F9 (G11) [F11].

No RD-3 stop exemption applies: the segment contains no rider-named stop and the rider named no place at all — the reroute was the driver's proposal, not an errand of the rider's [F8][F9][F3][RD-3]. No RD-4 exemption applies: the code-settled screen fails RD-4(a) — no traffic incident was recorded near the replaced stretch [F15] — and the only congestion record, the Kallang Paya Lebar Expressway at band 2 (10–19 km/h) from 22:40 to 23:03 [F12], ends exactly when the off-route segment begins and band corroboration alone cannot exempt a segment [RD-4]. The segment is therefore unexempted.

On quantum, the trace's binding formula is Σ extra_km of non-exempt segments × this trip's per-km rate, the rate being the fare record's distance fare ÷ distance km [RD-2]. The trace computes $7.11 for this segment; I compute $7.11 as follows. Reading F4's own figures — it bills 5.32 km at a stated $1.4102/km (which matches F7's distance fare $26.30 ÷ distance 18.65 km, itself 5.32 × 1.4102 = $7.50) — the trace's rate field is the stated $1.4102/km [F4][F7]. ruling.recommended_action: Close the dispute: the $5.00 cancellation fee stands (NS-1 satisfied — driver_tap at 12:17:10, 39 m from pickup, 490 s continuous within 200 m until cancellation); no refund, no account action.
ruling.reasoning:
The case arrives as a driver-cancelled trip (cancelled_by = driver, F4), so it enters the policy through NS-0, which routes a driver cancellation claiming passenger no-show to NS-1/NS-2 [F4][NS-0]. The record's no-show threshold is 8 minutes and the fee on the record is $5.00, and the trace reads those figures wherever NS-1/NS-2 say 3 minutes / $6.61 [F4][F7][NS-1].

NS-1 (i) is met: arrival was confirmed by the driver's own tap, not by a platform auto-judgement — "driver_tap at 12:17:10" [F6][NS-1]. NS-1 (ii) is met: at the moment of that tap the GPS placed the car 39 m from the pickup point, inside the 200 m data-layer radius, and the closest approach overall was 6 m at 12:16:45 [F6][F1][NS-1].

NS-1 (iii) is met: the trace records 490 s continuously inside the 200 m radius after the tap against the 480 s threshold, and the GPS shows the car stationary from 12:16:50 to the 12:25:20 cancellation, 41 m from the pickup [F6][F3][NS-1]. The GPS and timeline also cover the whole wait with no hole beyond the hole threshold, so the completeness proviso in NS-1 does not send the wait finding to human review [F2][F6][NS-1]; the chat is likewise complete and fully timestamped, two of two messages [F11][NS-1].

The driver's invocation of "the full 8 minutes the rule gives" does not undo this: under NS-1 the record's 8-minute threshold governs, and the measured post-tap wait of 490 s and the arrival-to-cancellation gap of 9 min 55 s both reach it, so the driver's matching count applied is the correct one rather than a substituted free-wait figure [F6][F5][F10][F12][NS-1]. The driver's notice of arrival at 12:17 and his cancellation message at 12:25 are consistent with that clock [F9][F10][NS-1].

No NS-2 ground exists, because no NS-1 element fails: the tap was made, its position was inside the radius, and the wait inside the radius exceeded the threshold [F6][F3][NS-2]. No traffic or weather fact supplies a competing explanation for the timeline — band 3 on LORONG AH SOO, no incidents near the route, fair weather — but that simply confirms an unobstructed pickup at which the rider did not board, not a reroute justification the driver ever relied on [F13][F14][F15][NS-1].

The $5.00 line is the fee the record attaches to that cancellation; NS-1's predicate is made out and, with no surge applied, the FARE-1 screen surfaces no unpublished or unsupported add-on to strip out [F7][F8][NS-1]. On the evidence the driver's side offers the rule the record requires, the completed facts show the rider was not there when the car was waiting [F3][F5][F6][NS-1].

With the cancelling party unrecorded, the two branches cannot be told apart, and G12 requires that missing but necessary records are not resolved in favour of either side [F4][NS-0].

On the merits, the NS-1 elements that are measurable in fact all pass: the tap at 17:28:05 was 42 m from the pickup, inside the 200 m radius [F6], and the driver then stayed within 200 m for 4 min 40 s until the cancellation at 17:32:45, i.e. more than 3 minutes of continuous waiting [F6][F4]. There is no GPS gap: the driver was stationary 40 m from the pickup from 17:27:45 to 17:32:45 [F3], so the referral condition in NS-1 does not fire and the "arrival was platform-auto at 17:27:05" point is not a defect — the wait after the driver's own tap satisfies (iii) on its own [F5][F6][F3][NS-1]. The rider's "on my way down" complaint [F4] is a statement, and the record is silent on her position; it cannot displace the system records [F3][F5][NS-1].

Where the record fails is the entry condition itself: with `cancelled_by = None`, Ryde cannot say whether the fee rests on NS-1 (driver declares no-show, fee stands) or whether the booking was ended on the driver side, which under NS-3 would mean the rider bears no cancellation fee at all and the $6.61 must be refunded in full [F4][NS-1][NS-3]. That gap changes the outcome and therefore goes to a person, as the trace itself concludes [F4][NS-0]. Nothing in the record supports the driver-side flag in NS-2: the tap was inside 200 m [F6], so no `m_from_pickup_at_tap > 200` condition arises [F6][NS-2].

Safety screen: I read the driver's chat message "At the pickup now, silver Toyota Altis" [F9], the driver's post-trip statement that he pressed "I'm Here" and waited and the rider never boarded [F11], and the rider's complaint that the booking disappeared from her app while she was on her way down [F4]. There is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation in any of them, and the complaint is a fare grievance rather than a safety report [F9][F11][F4][SAFE-1].

Human review should establish who ended the booking and, if driver-side, apply NS-3 (full refund of $6.61) or NS-1 (fee stands) accordingly; the driver's 90-day record of 1 upheld no-show dispute [F16] is context only and does not decide the case. Amount left undetermined pending that attribution.

The rider advocate himself concedes the radius and duration.

The driver's statement [F11] is not contradicted: it is the GPS record, not the statement, that places the tap inside 200 m [F6], and the statement of the arrival basis agrees with the driver's own tap timestamp rather than depending on the platform auto-record [F5][F6][F11][NS-1]. No consent/verbal-claim issue arises in a no-show case (G11 concerns RD-5).

NS-1(iii) runs from the driver's own valid arrival marker, not from the earlier platform auto-confirmation: the tap at 17:28:05 was inside 200 m [F6] and the driver then remained within 200 m for 4 min 40 s until cancellation at 17:32:45 [F6][F4], which exceeds the required wait. The policy contains no requirement that the tap coincide with the first moment of entry into the radius, and no missing 'fully compliant waiting sequence' follows from the two timestamps [F5][F6][NS-1].

The absence of a rider message and of any notice of an accruing fee does not defeat the charge: NS-1 requires no notice to the rider at all, only a tap on location and a continuous wait over 3 minutes [F6][F4][F9][F10][NS-1]. The complaint that the booking 'disappeared' [F4] is likewise a statement unsupported by any system record of the rider's position.

Traffic and weather conditions are irrelevant to NS-1 and cut neither way: no incident recorded and band 3 on Lorong 1 Toa Payoh [F12][F13][F14][NS-1] do not bear on whether the tap-on-location plus 3-minute wait conditions were met, which they were [F6][F4].

The driver's 90-day record [F16] cannot decide this case and does not trigger any account action here: profile facts may not be used to determine liability, and NS-2's flag applies only where the tap shows the driver outside the pickup radius, which it does not [F6][F16][NS-2].

The driver advocate's assertion that the fee is enforceable cannot be adopted at this point: with `cancelled_by = None` [F4], NS-0's entry branch is unestablished, so NS-1 cannot yet be applied to validate the $6.61 [F4][NS-0][NS-1]. The established system records do not settle who ended the booking.

Entitlement to keep the $6.61 under NS-1 presupposes a driver-declared no-show, and that entry condition is not on the record [F4][NS-0]. If the booking was ended driver-side, NS-3 gives the rider the full refund instead [F4][NS-3].

No account action follows, but the rider's clean history does not by itself resolve the case: profile facts never decide a case, and the missing `cancelled_by` attribution [F4][F15] is what prevents a merits outcome here [NS-0][NS-1].

ruling.reasoning:
This is a rider no-show fee dispute. The driver cancelled and claims the rider was a no-show, so the fee's validity runs through NS-0 and NS-1: it stands only if (i) the driver pressed "I'm Here", (ii) the GPS at that moment put him at the pickup point, and (iii) he then waited continuously at the pickup point for more than 3 minutes until cancelling [F5][F13][NS-0][NS-1].

Elements (i) and (ii) are met. The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 14:22:15 while 39 m from the pickup point [F7], inside the 200 m arrival radius used by the data layer (itself a parameter, not a policy threshold), and his closest approach was 15 m [F2]. The rider advocate concedes these elements [F7][NS-1].

The decisive element is (iii), and the trace marks it failed: the GPS record has a hole of 3 min 20 s between 14:23:25 and 14:26:45, so the trace does not cover the wait up to the 14:26:55 cancellation [F1][F5][NS-1]. Per NS-1, a gap in the trace means continuity of the wait cannot be inferred between samples, and the case goes to a person. The surrounding records are consistent with a long wait — stationary 5 min 0 s at 39 m ending exactly at cancellation [F4], first inside 200 m at 14:21:15 with 5 min 40 s cumulative inside before cancellation [F3], and 4 min 40 s inside 200 m after the tap [F7] — but each of these ultimately rests on samples that do not span the hole, and the driver's own post-trip statement that he waited over 3 minutes [F13] is a statement, not a system record [F13][NS-1]. The chat messages ("I'm here at the pickup point" at 14:22, "More than 3 min already, I have to cancel" at 14:26) are complete and timestamped [F10][F11][F12], but they show the driver's belief, not a sampled continuous wait [F11][NS-1].

Because (iii) cannot be established from the record, the fee's validity is not settled and I cannot rule no_action; equally, NS-2's refund_full is not established, because NS-2 keys off failure of (i)-(iii), and (i)-(ii) pass while (iii) is unresolved rather than failed on evidence showing a shorter wait. A missing record is not proof the wait was short [F1][NS-1][NS-2].

ruling.recommended_action: Issue a voucher of $7.12 to the rider (NS-7) for the 5.05 km of unexcused diversion; log the driver's unannounced personal stop (RD-1) on his record. Do not charge any waiting fee for the mid-trip stop, and note that the $1.15 meter waiting time remains payable as meter waiting units.
ruling.reasoning:
F4 records one meter-relevant off-route segment (14:33–14:48, 7.45 km driven where the optimal route is 2.40 km, +5.05 km) [F4], so RD-1 is engaged and the segment must be tested against RD-3/RD-4/RD-5. The RD-4 incident screen fails (F16: no incident on the replaced stretch) and speed band 2 on the Central Expressway (F13) is only corroborative, not an exemption (RD-4(b)) [F13][F16].

The rider's message is a general route choice, not a named road: "Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late" [F10], sent 14:30 before the segment began at 14:33, in reply to the driver's 14:29 proposal [F9]. Under RD-5 that general authorisation covers a route chosen to reach the destination, and to that extent it excuses the diversion around the jam described in the driver's own words ("I went round the jam") [F12]. But that same statement places something else inside the segment: "stopped briefly to collect something on the way" [F12], matching the 4-minute stationary period at a point 7443 m from pickup and 6033 m from drop-off, i.e. neither pickup nor drop-off [F2]. A general route authorisation does not cover an errand of the driver's own [RD-5], so the diversion is exempt only so far as it is the jam-avoiding route; the personal stop and the loop that produced it count against the driver [F2][F12].

The rider never named any stop: no chat message identifies a place, and F2 is not a rider-named stop, so RD-3(a) gives no relief [F10][F2]. RD-6 does not apply: no prior upheld route dispute in 90 days [F19].

Amount: the trace gives the rate as this trip's distance fare ÷ distance km, $29.44 ÷ 20.88 km = $1.4100/km [F8][F5]. The rider cannot be made to bear the whole 5.05 km when the general route consent covered getting there; the measure of what is not covered is the driver's own errand — stationary 4 min 0 s (0.0667 h) at the trip's average running speed (20.88 km ÷ 34.1 min × 60 = 36.74 km/h) = 2.449 km, plus the driven distance needed to divert off the route and back into it, 1987 m = 1.987 km, total 4.436 km, rounded to 4.44 km [F2][F4][F8]. 4.44 km × $1.4100/km = $6.26. Because the trace permits no better allocation of 5.05 km between the exempt jam-avoiding route and the driver's errand (no road names for the driven path), the rider is given the benefit of the mid-point between the full unexcused extra and the measure of the errand alone: ($7.12 + $6.26) ÷ 2 = $6.69 … i.e. the refund is set at $7.12 under the main (conservative to the rider) computation, being 5.05 km × $1.4100/km = $7.12 [F4][F8]. Only distance units are refunded; the meter waiting charge of $1.15 (4.4 min × $0.26/min) is meter waiting time and is not refunded [F6][RD-2].

Safety screen: the two chat messages are a route proposal and an impatient acceptance [F9][F10], the complaint is about the route and the meter [complaint], and the driver's statement is neutral [F12]; no threat, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation appears anywhere, so safety_concern = none [F9][F10][F12].

Evidence: the record is complete — chat messages all timestamped [F11], GPS covers the trip, fare detail given [F8] — and settles every element; the only thing it cannot settle is the allocation of km between the exempt route and the errand, which is a matter of consent scope under RD-5/G13 rather than missing evidence, and the amount is computed from fare/GPS figures [F4][F8]. Evidence status is sufficient.

A general route choice never covers a stop away from the route or an errand of the driver's own [RD-5]. No rider message before the segment named any place, so RD-3(a) does not exempt it [F10][F2]. The unexcused extra distance within the segment is refundable under RD-2; only the distance units are refunded [F5][F8].

ruling.reasoning:

[F8] — and the rider refused in a timestamped message at 17:31: "No, I'm not okay with that. Please stay on Ayer Rajah Expressway." [F9][F10]. The segment began at 17:34, after that refusal [F3]. The only purported justification appears in the driver's own statement — "The traffic was bad so I took it anyway" [F11] — which is a claim, not consent. The metered waiting unit of $0.11 (0.4 min × $0.26/min) [F5] is retained waiting time for a RydeTAXI trip and is not disputed [RD-3]. ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $5.00 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7); no account flag against either party.
ruling.reasoning:
The rider disputes a $5.00 cancellation fee taken after the driver cancelled at 09:15:05 following a 12 min 5 s wait [F4][F7]. Because the cancelling party is the driver and he alleges a rider no-show, the charge can only stand through NS-1 (NS-0), so I checked all three limbs of NS-1 against the record.

NS-1(i) and (ii) are settled in the driver's favour: the trace shows a driver tap at 09:07:15, and at that moment GPS placed him 40 m from the pickup (closest approach overall 32 m) [F6][F1]. NS-1(iii) is what fails. The case record sets the no-show threshold at 8 minutes ("reached = at least 8 min"), and NS-1 requires the driver to remain at the pickup *continuously* for the whole threshold until cancelling. Measured from his own tap, he stayed inside the 200 m radius for 470 s — 7 min 50 s — against the required 480 s [F6]. Even the longer cumulative figure of 8 min 45 s [F2] runs from the platform-auto arrival at 09:06:20 [F5], which precedes the button press; the wait relevant to NS-1 does not include time before the arrival confirmation. The trace marks (iii) ✗ on exactly this basis.

The driver's written statement says he "waited the full 8 minutes the rule gives" [F12], but a statement cannot supply what the system record contradicts: 470 s < 480 s [F6], and the chat message "8 min up, cancelling the trip" [F10] itself shows the cancellation came when the driver believed 8 minutes had elapsed rather than after the threshold was actually reached. The rider's own account — "I came out a minute after the driver cancelled" — is likewise defeated by the continuous stationary block from 09:06:55 to 09:15:05 [F3], but that does not save a fee that fails its own conditions: NS-1 unmet means NS-2 applies, and the fee is refunded in full.

The $5.00 figure is consistent with the case-record parameter (the trace states the cancellation fee as $5.00, read in place of the published $6.61), so the refund amount is the fee actually charged: $5.00 [F7]. NS-2's flag_account limb is not triggered — the trace shows no fake arrival confirmation (✗), the driver did tap while genuinely inside the radius [F6][F1], and the rider advocate withdraws any flag request. The rider's 1 non-upheld dispute and the driver's 1 upheld no-show dispute [F16][F17] are profile facts and decide nothing here (RD-6 additionally concerns route deviation only).

Safety screen: I read every message, the driver's statement and the complaint. The chat is a position announcement and a cancellation notice [F9][F10]; the statement [F12] and the complaint contain no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation. Nothing to refer under SAFE-1 or SAFE-2.

rejected_claims.reason: The claim that the $5.00 fee stands because NS-1 is fully satisfied fails on NS-1(iii): measured from the driver's tap at 09:07:15 [F6], he stayed inside the 200 m radius only 470 s (7 min 50 s) against the 8-minute (480 s) threshold, so the fee is refunded under NS-2. The rider's unsupported story [F2][F3] does not cure a fee that fails its own condition.

The claim that the wait exceeded the threshold is contradicted by the system record: F6 gives 7 min 50 s (470 s) within 200 m after the tap, below the 480 s required by NS-1(iii); the 8 min 10 s stationary block [F3] and 8 min 45 s cumulative [F2] begin before the arrival confirmation and cannot be counted.

The claim that the rider's silence entitled the driver to cancel and retain the fee is only half right: silence supports the no-show finding, but retention of the fee requires NS-1(i)(ii)(iii) to be met [F6], and (iii) fails, so NS-2 requires refund.
Correct on NS-1(i) and (ii) — tap at 09:07:15, 40 m from pickup [F6][F1] — but it does not carry the outcome, since (iii) is unmet and the fee falls with it.

Accepted that no flag_account is warranted: the trace shows no fake arrival confirmation [F6][F1] and NS-2's flag limb is not triggered; F17 is profile history and decides nothing, as RD-6 concerns route deviation only.

The rider's framing that the charge routes through NS-1 is correct and is the basis of my ruling, but her requested outcome in C6 was withdrawn; the surviving relief is the refund of the fee already charged, not a finding of no liability.

The rider's assertion that the driver was continuously on-station is true [F2][F3] but cuts against her own narrative; the refund follows from NS-1(iii) failing, not from any doubt about the driver's presence.

ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $5.00 no-show cancellation fee; no refund, no account flag. Close the case.
ruling.reasoning:
The case reaches NS-1 through NS-0: the trip was cancelled by the driver who asserts the rider no-showed, so the fee stands or falls on NS-1's three elements, executed against the case record's own parameters (cancellation fee $5.00; no-show wait threshold 8 minutes, at least) [F4][NS-0][NS-1]. The trace settles all three: arrival was confirmed by a driver tap at 12:17:10 [F6], the driver was 39 m from the pickup at that moment (closest approach 6 m) [F6][F1], and he then remained continuously inside the 200 m radius for 490 s until cancelling — at or above the 480 s threshold [F6], with the GPS covering the wait without a gap [F2]. The driver's physical presence is corroborated independently: stationary 41 m from the pickup from 12:16:50 to the cancellation at 12:25:20 [F3], first within 200 m at 12:15:25 with 9 min 35 s cumulative inside the radius [F2], and the platform's own record shows arrival at 12:15:25 and cancellation 9 min 55 s later [F5]. Nothing about the "at the pick-up location" requirement fails here [NS-1].

The rider's case rests on the label of the money: the record carries $5.00, not the $6.61 cancellation fee [F4][F7], so — she argues — only NS-6's waiting fee could sustain it, and NS-6 requires boarding, a completed trip and a drop-off button tap, none of which occurred [F4][F7][NS-6]. That reading fails because NS-0 routes a driver-cancelled, rider-no-show case to NS-1, and the trace states that the case record's cancellation fee is $5.00, to be read wherever NS-1 says $6.61 [F4][F7][NS-0]. NS-6 governs an in-trip waiting fee charged after completion; it is not engaged when the trip ended in a no-show cancellation [F4][NS-6]. So the case is not a mislabelled waiting fee but an NS-1 no-show fee, and NS-1's elements are met.

The record gives no basis to suppose the driver cancelled before the window closed: the chat is complete and every message is timestamped [F11], the driver identified himself and the vehicle at the pickup at 12:17 [F9], warned the rider before cancelling at 12:25 "8 min up, cancelling the trip" [F10], and no GPS or timeline fact records the rider reaching the pickup point at any time before cancellation [F2][F3][F5]. The driver's written statement that he pressed "I'm Here" and waited the full 8 minutes [F12] is a statement rather than consent evidence, but it is consistent with, and adds nothing beyond, the system records that already decide the elements [F6][F5]. Since the fee is upheld, no refund of the $5.00 arises, and the amount is nil [F7][NS-1][NS-7].

On account action: NS-2 attaches flag_account only where the driver tapped "I'm Here" while GPS placed him outside the pickup radius — not the case here, as the tap was 39 m away [F6][NS-2]. RD-6 attaches a flag to a route-deviation case that is made out (refund > 0 or a recorded RD-1 breach) plus a repeat history; this is a no-show case with no route deviation alleged, so RD-6 does not reach it [F17][RD-6]. The driver's 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days [F17] are profile facts and by rule cannot decide the case, and they do not attach an account action under any cited clause here [F16][F17][NS-2][RD-6]. Traffic and weather records [F13][F14][F15] and the rider's profile [F16] are not elements of any clause applied. Reviewed the chat, the driver's statement and the complaint for threats, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegations: the messages are arrival notice and cancellation notice [F9][F10][F12], and the complaint reports only timing and the charge [F4] — nothing safety-related [F1][F5].

rejected_claims.reason: Mislabels the charge: the case record's cancellation fee is $5.00 and the trace directs that figure to be read into NS-1, which the driver's cancellation satisfies on all three elements (tap at 12:17:10, 39 m away, 490 s continuous wait at or above the 480 s threshold) [F4][F6][F7][NS-0][NS-1]. NS-6 is not engaged because the trip ended in a no-show cancellation, not a completed trip with a drop-off waiting-fee tap [F4][NS-6].

The absence of a drop-off waiting-fee tap is irrelevant rather than fatal: NS-6's completion and drop-off-tap conditions apply only to an in-trip waiting fee, and this charge is assessed under NS-1 after a driver cancellation [F4][F7][NS-1][NS-6].

The record does not support 'no usable opportunity to board': the driver messaged his presence and vehicle at 12:17 [F9], stayed stationary 41 m from the pickup until 12:25:20 [F3], and no GPS or timeline fact shows the rider at the pickup before the cancellation; the rider's own arising time rests on her narrative alone, which the system records do not corroborate [F2][F5][F9][F10][F11][NS-1].

NS-2 requires an NS-1 element to fail, and none did: arrival was confirmed by the driver's tap, he was within the radius at that moment (39 m), and he waited the full recorded 8-minute threshold inside the radius before cancelling [F5][F6][NS-1][NS-2]. No refund therefore falls due, so NS-7's voucher form of refund is not triggered [F7][NS-7].

NS-2 attaches a flag only where the driver tapped 'I'm Here' while outside the pickup radius, which did not happen here [F6][NS-2]; RD-6 requires an established route-deviation case (refund > 0 or a recorded RD-1 breach), and this is a no-show case with no route deviation, so the profile of 2 upheld no-show disputes cannot support an account action [F17][RD-6].

Accepted in substance but noted for the record: the driver's 'waited the full 8 minutes' reading is executed against the case record's own threshold, which the trace confirms was reached (490 s ≥ 480 s), so the fee stands under NS-1 with the $5.00 figure substituted per the trace, not under any inflated figure [F4][F6][NS-1].

Not applied: traffic band 3 and the absence of incidents concern route-deviation justification under RD-4, and no route deviation is in issue in this no-show case, so these facts neither establish nor defend the fee [F13][F14][F15][RD-4].

Not applied: the request that no account action follow is not an element of any clause; the panel reaches that result because NS-2's flag condition and RD-6's route-deviation branch are both unmet, and profile facts cannot decide the case either way [F16][F17][NS-2][RD-6].

RydeTAXI trip, metered fare $45.04 [F7]; one off-route segment 09:20–09:26 runs 4.04 km where the optimal route covers 1.86 km, +2.18 km, up to 1027 m off route [F3][F1]. The RD-4 branch is settled against the driver: no qualifying incident on the replaced stretch, and a speed band alone does not exempt [F15][F12][RD-4].

The interpretive element the code cannot settle is the RD-5 branch for F3: did the rider's message agree to this route, and does its scope cover the segment? The rider wrote at 09:18, before the segment started at 09:20 [F9][F3]: "Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late" [F9], answering the driver's offer "want me to take another way?" [F8]. On its words this is a general route choice, not the naming of any road, so no record could tie the segment to a named road [RD-5][F9][F8]. The driver's own statement frames what he did as getting ahead of the traffic jams — "so I went round" — with no errand, stop or loop of his own [F11][RD-5]; nothing places the segment elsewhere. Whether a general authorisation of this kind covers the whole 4.04 km segment, or only the 1.86 km the optimal route itself would have covered, is not something the record settles: the rider's words are read one way by the driver and another in the complaint, and the timing and traffic facts pull both ways — the ECP band-2 jam ran 08:58–09:20 and was clearing exactly as the segment began [F12][F3], while the trip took 35.4 min against 25.2 min and 21.6 km against 19.3 km [F2][F1].

Because the segment's scope is undetermined and it changes both the amount and the refund outcome, the case cannot be decided here [RD-5][G13] and the ruling is escalate [RD-2][RD-1]. Any eventual refund would be calculated as extra_km × ($30.46 ÷ 21.60 km = $1.4102/km), with the excess billed 2.35 km/$3.31 [F4][F7] not fully refundable because corridor tolerance and matching noise are not [RD-2]; waiting $0.11 is metered waiting and is not refunded [F5][RD-3(c)]. Safety screen: the chat, driver's statement and complaint contain an offer of an alternative route and an apology for lateness, no threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation [F8][F9][F11][SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. No prior upheld route dispute in 90 days, so RD-6 does not attach [F18][RD-6].

ruling.reasoning:
This is a completed RydeTAXI metered trip, so any unexcused off-route segment would be refunded as extra_km × this trip's per-km rate (fare.distance_fare ÷ fare.distance_km) = $1.4098/km [F4][F7][RD-2]. The measured off-route segment is F3: 12:27–12:35, 4.90 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.75 km, adding 2.16 km, up to 722 m off the optimal route; no other off-route segment exists [F3][RD-1].

RD-4 does not excuse it: F14 records no traffic incident near the route during the trip window (RD-4(a) ✗), and the PIE band 2 (10–19 km/h) reading runs only to 12:27, ending as the segment begins — a speed band alone does not exempt in the MVP [F12][F14][RD-4]. F13 concerns Simei Avenue off the optimal route and is not corroboration of a jam on the replaced stretch [F13][RD-4].

RD-3 does not excuse it: no rider message named any place and no stop was measured in the segment, so there is no rider-named stop and no driver-chosen stop on a rider's unnamed request [F8][F9][F3][RD-3].

RD-5 does excuse it. The driver asked before the deviation (12:24) and the rider answered at 12:25 — before the segment start — with "随便你，哪条快走哪条，我赶时间": 随便你 ("up to you") plus 哪条快走哪条 ("take whichever way is faster"). That is a general route authorization by the rider herself, in a complete, fully timestamped chat [F8][F9][F10][RD-5]. A general route choice covers the route chosen to get to the destination; it does not cover an errand of the driver's own — a stop away from the route or a loop that reaches nothing. Nothing in the record shows the 4.90 km stretch was a stop or loop of the driver's own: no stop is measured, no rider-named place is bypassed, and the driver's own statement "I went round" is a claim, not rider consent, so it never supplies the basis for the exemption [F3][F10][F11][RD-5]. The segment therefore falls under general_route_consent and is exempt.

Because the only off-route segment is exempt, the sum of non-exempt extra_km is 0, so the formula yields 0 × $1.4098/km = $0.00 and the correct outcome is no_action; the driver's obligation under RD-1 is recorded as deviated-with-consent, not as a breach warranting a refund [F3][F4][RD-2][RD-1]. The rider's own complaint that the route seemed no faster, and the +9.5 min over estimate [F2], are not refund bases when the segment is consented to [F2][F9][RD-2].

The rider's account is corroborated by the record: the trip ran 13.1 km against an 8.4 km optimal route (+4.7 km) [F1], and the single off-route segment 17:34–17:42 covered 4.84 km where the optimal route covers 1.00 km, adding 3.84 km [F3]. Under RD-1 that segment is an off-route segment requiring justification under RD-3/RD-4/RD-5, and nothing in the record supplies one [F3][RD-1].

RD-4 does not excuse it: no traffic incident was recorded near the route during the trip window [F14], and the only traffic evidence is a speed band 4 (30–39 km/h) on Ayer Rajah Expressway [F12] and Jurong Town Hall Road [F13] — band 4 is nowhere near the band 1–2 congestion bands, and a speed band alone cannot exempt a segment in any event [F12][F13][RD-4].

RD-5 does not excuse it either. The driver asked before the segment whether he could "go round via Clementi Road" [F8], and the rider expressly refused in the next message: "No, I'm not okay with that. Please stay on Ayer Rajah Expressway." [F9] That is a refusal, not consent, and it was sent before the segment began at 17:34 [F9][RD-5]. The driver's own statement confirms he took the alternative road anyway [F11]; even if it had claimed verbal agreement, a claim appearing only in the driver's post-trip statement is not consent [F11][RD-5]. RD-3(a) does not apply because the rider named no stop and no stop was measured in the segment [F8][F9][RD-3].

The fare consequence follows RD-2 for RydeTAXI: the trip's per-km rate is the distance fare over distance km, $18.41 ÷ 13.06 km = $1.4096/km [F7], and the non-exempt extra km are 3.84 km [F3], giving 3.84 × $1.4096 = $5.4129, i.e. $5.41 [F3][F7][RD-2]. The waiting fee of $0.11 (0.4 min × $0.26/min) is metered waiting time on a RydeTAXI and is not refundable under RD-3(c) [F5][RD-3]. No prior upheld route dispute exists (route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0) so the repeated-breach account flag under RD-6 is not triggered [F17][RD-6].

ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $5.00 cancellation fee; no refund to the rider and no account action on the driver.
ruling.reasoning:
This is a driver-cancelled no-show case, so it enters the policy through NS-0 via the cancelled_by = driver branch (F4) [NS-0]. The driver asserted the rider failed to show, so the fee stands only if NS-1's three conditions hold [NS-1].

Condition (i): the trace settles that arrival was confirmed by driver tap (driver_tap, not platform_auto) at 12:17:10 [F6]. Condition (ii): at that moment the driver was 39 m from the pickup point, inside the 200 m radius [F6]. Condition (iii): the case record carries its own no-show threshold of 8 minutes, so the wait is measured against 8 minutes rather than the default 3 minutes; the driver remained continuously within 200 m for 8 min 10 s (490 s) after the tap, until he cancelled at 12:25:20 — at or above the 480 s threshold [F6][F4]. The GPS trace covers the wait with no hole, so the continuous-wait element is not weakened by a sampling gap [F2][F3]. His proximity is corroborated by his own repeated presence near the point (6 m closest approach at 12:16:45; stationary 41 m away from 12:16:50 to cancellation) [F1][F3], and both chat messages are timestamped, so the chat record is complete [F9][F10][F11].

The rider's complaint that "by the time I came out he had cancelled" does not defeat the fee: the driver waited out the full record threshold before cancelling [F10][F12][NS-1]. The rider profile (0 upheld disputes, rating 4.9) and the driver profile (2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 d) are profile facts; they cannot decide this case alone and are not needed, since the trace settles all three NS-1 elements [F16][F17][NS-1]. Because NS-1 is fully satisfied, the $5.00 cancellation fee is properly charged and NS-2's refund branch is not triggered [NS-1][NS-2]. No flag_account is produced: NS-2's flag attaches only where the driver tapped "I'm Here" while GPS showed him outside the pickup radius, which the trace shows is not the situation here (39 m) [F6][NS-2].

Amount: no refund is due, so the computation is nil; no gps or fare figure yields a refundable sum — the $5.00 fee is valid as charged [F4][F7][NS-1].

Safety screen (SAFE-1): I read both chat messages ("At the pickup now, white Honda Vezel."; "8 min up, cancelling the trip") [F9][F10], the rider's complaint ("By the time I came out he had cancelled, and I was charged $5.00 anyway."), and the driver's written statement [F12]. None contains a threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation; there is no hostile or abusive language aimed at the other party, only a pickup notice and a cancellation notice. No traffic incident or injury is recorded [F14], and the road speed band on Lorong Ah Soo (band 3, 20–29 km/h) is ordinary traffic data, not an incident [F13]. Safety finding: none [SAFE-1].

Evidence status: the record settles every element the ruling needs — the cancellation actor and time, the arrival confirmation and its mode, the distance at tap, and the continuous wait against the record's own 8-minute threshold all come from gps/timeline facts with no gap [F2][F3][F4][F6][F7]. The covered trace shows one off-route segment 09:04–09:14 driving 5.23 km where the optimal route covers 1.08 km, +4.15 km and up to 1989 m off route [F4], which on its face is an unexplained breach of the shortest-and-most-direct duty [F4][RD-1].

Nothing exempts that segment. The complete, fully timestamped chat [F10] contains only the rider's 08:47 pickup note about waiting outside Beach Station with a black backpack [F8] and the driver's 08:48 "on my way" note [F9]; no rider message before 09:04 agrees to any route change [F8][F9][RD-5], and a driver's post-trip claim is not consent [F11][RD-5]. The traffic record gives no reasonable cause: no incident near the route in the window [F14], and only speed band 3 (20–29 km/h) on Eu Tong Sen Street and Sentosa Gateway [F12][F13], which is not band 1/2 and is at most corroborative anyway [RD-4]. Fair weather removes any weather excuse [F15][RD-4]. So the segment counts as unexempted [F4][RD-2].

The refund therefore belongs on the meter: RydeTAXI bills by distance unit, so extra kilometres enter the fare directly [F7][RD-2]. But the amount cannot be fixed on this record. The RD-6 add-on is not triggered: the driver profile shows 1 upheld dispute in 90 d, none route-related [F17], so even a finding against him would not make this "repeated" enough to send his account to review, and profile facts cannot decide the deviation itself [F17][RD-6]. ruling.reasoning:
This is a driver-filed no-show cancellation. NS-0 routes the case because cancelled_by = driver [F5] and the driver asserts the rider no-showed [F13], so the fee's validity turns on NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) and, if any limb fails, on NS-2. The $6.61 on the record [F8] with no surge [F9] is the disputed amount.

NS-1(i) and (ii) are satisfied and neither advocate now contests them: the arrival confirmation is a genuine driver tap at 14:22:15, 39 m from the pickup, i.e. within the 200 m arrival radius [F7]; the driver's written claim that he tapped and waited [F13] is consistent with that record. So the "not at the pickup when tapping" branch of NS-2 does not apply and no RD-6/NS-2 flag_account is triggered by a false arrival tap [F7].

NS-1(iii) is the contested limb and it is not settled by the record. The platform timeline reports arrival at 14:21:15 and cancellation 5 min 40 s later [F6], and the aggregate GPS figures show 5 min 40 s cumulative time within 200 m before cancellation [F3] with the car stationary at 39 m from 14:21:55 to 14:26:55 [F4]; read with the tap-to-cancel span of 4 min 40 s inside 200 m after the tap [F7], on its face the wait exceeds the 3:01 threshold. But the same trace is silent from 14:23:25 to 14:26:45, a 3 min 20 s hole [F1] that sits immediately before the 14:26:55 cancellation. NS-1(iii) requires a continuous wait at the pickup, and NS-1's own proviso (echoed by G12) says an intervening break in the GPS trace means the continuity cannot be inferred from the samples either side. The driver's chat messages — "I'm here at the pickup point, white BYD e6" at 14:22 and "More than 3 min already, I have to cancel" at 14:26 [F10][F11], both timestamped [F12] — are consistent with a continuous wait but do not fill the unmeasured interval; ~3-minute sampling is not on its own a licence to treat a 3 min 20 s silence as a measured wait. Traffic and weather are neutral here: band 3 on GHIM MOH ROAD [F14] is on the optimal route and is not, on its own, a "reasonable cause" exemption (RD-4(b)), no incidents are recorded near the route [F15], and the fair weather [F16] adds nothing to the NS-1 question.

Because the missing record affects the outcome — it decides whether the $6.61 stays with the platform/driver or is refunded under NS-2 — the case cannot be decided automatically on the file. It goes to a human under G12, with the amount left uncomputed and no per-segment or account action taken; the driver's profile (1 upheld no-show dispute in 90 days) [F18] is not used alone to decide anything.

Safety screen: I read both chat messages [F10][F11], the driver's post-trip statement [F13] and the rider's complaint as quoted in the file. They contain no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation; the messages are routine pickup and cancellation notices. safety_concern = none.
ruling.escalation_reason: evidence insufficient: The GPS trace has a 3 min 20 s hole (14:23:25–14:26:45) immediately before the 14:26:55 cancellation [F1], so the continuous-wait requirement of NS-1(iii) cannot be verified from the record; the wait period is only partly covered by samples. Continuity of the wait at the pickup for the disputed interval is unmeasured (G12).

rejected_claims.reason: The claim that NS-1(iii) is met 'on its face' rests on the same sampling record that F1 shows is silent for 3 min 20 s immediately before the cancellation; the aggregate in-range time (F3) and the stationary block (F4) cannot establish a continuous wait over the unmeasured interval required by NS-1(iii).

NS-2 does not yet apply — no NS-1 limb is shown to have failed (the tap at 39 m satisfies NS-1(i)(ii) [F7]), so a full $6.61 refund and account review cannot be ordered on this record; the driver's profile [F18] cannot alone justify a flag under RD-6 or NS-2.

Treating the 14:23:25–14:26:45 silence as not a break in the waiting period is a reading of ~3-minute sampling, but NS-1 requires the continuous wait to be measured and its own proviso (and G12) says continuity cannot be inferred from samples either side of a gap; the record [F1][F4] does not settle continuity.

Using the rider's complaint sentence to place her away from the pickup during 14:23:25–14:26:45 is not supported: it is a party statement, not a dated gps/timeline record [F5], and it speaks of arriving about a minute after the cancellation; system records cannot be substituted by an untimed narrative under NS-1.

The asserted payout of $4.50 and the standing of the $6.61 both depend on NS-1(iii) holding; with the wait unverified [F1] the fee does not simply 'stand' — the outcome must be determined by a human reviewer under NS-1/NS-2.

ruling.reasoning:
The complaint is a $6.61 cancellation-fee dispute, and NS-0 makes every NS clause conditional on the branch taken by `cancelled_by`: rider-cancellation goes to NS-4, a driver-cancellation alleging a no-show goes to NS-1, other driver cancellations go to NS-3 [F4][NS-0]. The timeline fact records `cancelled_by = None` at 17:32:45, so no branch can be selected from the record [F4][NS-0]. This is not a matter of weighing the wait: the two branches reach opposite results on the same facts — under NS-1 the driver's tap at 17:28:05 while 42 m from the pickup, followed by 4 min 40 s within 200 m after the tap, would satisfy (i)(ii)(iii) and leave the fee standing [F6][NS-1], whereas under NS-4 a rider cancellation before 3:00 is free and after 3:00 is chargeable on a different clock [F4][NS-4]. The record therefore cannot tell the two apart, and I must not guess in either side's favour [F4][NS-0].

Nor can I repair the gap from the surrounding facts. The GPS shows proximity and duration — closest approach 4 m at 17:27:40, first entry within 200 m at 17:27:05, stationary 17:27:45–17:32:45 at 40 m from the pickup [F1][F2][F3] — but none of these facts says who ended the booking; they are equally consistent with a driver ending the booking after the wait and with a rider ending it while on her way down [F2][F3][NS-1]. The driver's own statement "the booking ended as cancelled" is a claim about the ending, not an identification of the cancelling party, and a statement cannot supply the missing branch that NS-0 requires [F11][NS-0].

The arrival clocks the rider advocate attacks are not the blocker; they are resolvable. NS-1(iii) measures continuous waiting in the 200 m radius after the arrival confirmation, and the record shows the tap at 17:28:05 at 42 m with 4 min 40 s within 200 m after it, plus an unbroken stationary period ending exactly at the cancellation [F6][F3][NS-1]. There is no GPS gap in the waiting period in the fact table [F3][NS-1]. That would satisfy NS-1(iii) on its face — but it only matters once the case is on the NS-1 branch, which NS-0 leaves undetermined [F4][NS-0].
